citations.quote: Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:

reading.distinction: Both prior models turn existence of a pending pre-effective application into a change-level removal veto. This rival distinguishes the substantive conditions attached to a change from the process attached to an application. A substantively qualifying change can coexist with an application that must follow the existing process. The prior models already identify the main actors and feature quantifiers; the consequential issue is the relation between application history and the legal effect being computed, including later application decisions.

facts.meaning: The assessed fund is either a UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, or a United Kingdom-domiciled collective investment scheme authorised as UK UCITS.

reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within scope, true means the identified change satisfies the substantive home-requirements and exception tests in item (ii); false means at least one of those tests fails. The result answers only that substantive question. It does not answer whether a pending application can leave the existing process or whether prior approval is legally required in the particular procedural circumstances. Outside scope no conclusion is supplied. Unknown facts remain unknown. This proposal confers no legal approval.
reading.subject: Substantive removal conditions distinguished from preservation of an application’s existing process

relationships: The management company proposes an investment change to the fund.
The fund’s domicile and authorisation classification determine coverage.
Home-jurisdiction requirements and feature exceptions attach to the identified change.
An application covers specified change components; application identity is distinct from change identity.
Receipt before the Effective Date and absence of a granted decision at transition determine preservation of the application’s existing process.
Later decisions change application status without changing the historical fact that it was pending at transition.
The supplied text does not specify the complete operational relationship between substantive removal and the preserved process.
proposals.temporal_basis: Assess substantive conditions on or after 28 November 2025. Separately record application receipt, decision status at that transition and subsequent decisions through the assessment date.
proposals.unit_of_assessment: One identified material investment change for substantive conditions, linked to separately identified applications and their decision histories for procedural treatment.

unresolved: The full selected question—whether prior SFC approval is required in the particular circumstances—remains unformalized. The missing FAQs and existing approval rules are needed to connect substantive qualification, preserved application processing and any outstanding approval obligation.
The rival does not establish that pending applications may bypass the existing process. It challenges treating preservation of that process as an express additional substantive exception.
Neither prior model supplies a rule for application closure, withdrawal, resubmission, overlapping applications or severability of bundled changes. The source does not justify inventing those rules.

The prior models place the Effective Date in different locations: one excludes earlier assessments from scope, while the other returns false within scope. Their outputs therefore answer different questions for pre-effective assessments.
